would_buy_zone.basis: Closes expectations_gap.rows[net_gap_direction] at the 5-year reverse-DCF convention (the tougher of the two the filed solve computes, and the one this dive's own gap claim rests on). Forward-solving quality.reverse_dcf's own growing-FCF-plus-Gordon-terminal-value formula (base_fcf $468.9M, 9% discount rate, 2.5% terminal growth, 5-year explicit horizon; this reconstruction reproduces the filed implied_fcf_cagr to three decimals at all three filed horizons: 32.963% vs filed 0.3296 at 5y, 24.386% vs filed 0.2439 at 7y, 18.337% vs filed 0.1834 at 10y) for a target g instead of solving for g: low=$148.13 is where the market's ask falls to this dive's own defended 10.67% five-year FCF-CAGR base case (net_gap_direction.mine); high=$162.54 is where it falls to a 13% stretch case (both derived from the same revenue-times-margin-times-conversion bridge in net_gap_direction, using EV = price x 72,000,000 FY2025 shares minus the file's own $232.9M net cash, the same bridge that reproduces today's $342.08 close exactly from the filed $24,629.76M market cap). Both bounds sit inside 0.3x-2.0x of the last close ($102.62-$684.16) and strictly below price_ref.value. RED TEAM (2026-09-06) bear-case stress: the zone's low ($148.13) is built on this file's own 'mine' net_gap_direction base case (7.5% revenue CAGR, percentile 65, already characterized in expectations_gap.rows[revenue_cagr_5y] as 'roughly at the top of the company's own previously stated long-term algorithm', not a bear case) and a 22% steady-state margin, also above the FY2025 GAAP level. Re-running the same bridge and forward-solve on an actual bear case, the trailing 3-year revenue CAGR this file itself cites (2.1%) with margin held flat at the FY2025 GAAP level (19.03%, no expansion), gives a fair price of $104.18 at the FY2025 cash-conversion ratio (0.8017) and $84.29 at the more volatile 4-year-average conversion ratio (0.6246), 29.7% to 43.1% BELOW this zone's own low end; even the guided FY2026 pace itself (9.38%) with no margin expansion prices the stock at $140.66, still below $148.13. This zone is therefore the price at which this dive's BASE case, not a haircut off the bear case, becomes fair value, and it does not survive an actual bear-case stress: a buyer at $148-162 is still paying for above-trend growth and margin expansion, with no demonstrated margin of safety against bear[0]-[1] actually playing out. The zone bounds are left unchanged because they correctly close this file's own gap-table row and every other WATCH zone in this analyst's log (VRT, HUBB, MYRG, ESLT) was drawn and left the same way; this finding instead corrects what the zone should be understood to represent (a base-case-fair floor, not a demonstrated bear-survived floor) and is escalated in this run's ledger and dive-log entry as a methodology question for Ron: whether method section 7's 'gap table AND bear case' wording for would_buy_zone requires the low bound itself to be a bear-case-survived price, which this zone, and by the same construction VRT's and MYRG's, is not.

priced_in_summary: WATCH on the COMPOUNDER clock. This is a real, disclosed, money-corner exposure (chain heat: impact 78, crowdedness 38, capture 72, verdict UNDISCOVERED) sitting over a mechanically clean earnings-quality core (Piotroski 8/9, Beneish -2.791 CLEAN, Altman 16.49 SAFE, net cash), and the FY2026 guide has been raised twice this year on genuine, disclosed reacceleration (HVP Delivery Devices +29.0% in Q1 2026; non-SmartDose-3.5 delivery devices growing 'double digits' in Q2, per the CFO). But the forward ask the price still embeds -- a 32.96% five-year implied FCF CAGR against this dive's own independently built 10.67% base case, a 22.29-point gap well outside this file's own 14.62-point horizon_spread -- survives only at the five-year convention: at the ten-year convention the implied ask (18.34%) sits only 7.67 points above this dive's estimate, inside the horizon_spread band, so by this file's own rule there is no measurable gap at that duration. Layered on that horizon-fragile gap: no figure anywhere on disk or disclosed attributes a specific GLP-1 or self-injection revenue share to this exact link (unlike the clean 10%-of-total-company figure disclosed for West's OTHER, CROWDED placement on this chain), and roughly a quarter of the disclosed device-platform revenue base (SmartDose 3.5mL, ~4% of FY2025 total company revenue) was sold to AbbVie mid-year, a real, sourced fact the market's extrapolation of Q1-Q2 growth rates does not appear to net out. Not TOO_LATE: FY2026 EPS guidance has been raised twice this year roughly in step with the price, which is an estimate-revision story rather than a pure multiple blow-off, and this dive's own log records six consecutive TOO_LATE declines precisely because the vocabulary requires demonstrated multiple EXPANSION eating the runway, not merely a rich forward multiple (38.2x on the FY2026 adjusted-EPS guide midpoint) sitting next to real numbers. Not INVESTABLE: the gap that would justify it is real only under the convention this dive considers the tougher, not the only defensible one, and the independence test's own falsification trigger (Q3 2026 results, late October) has not yet had a chance to fire in either direction.
bull: Real, disclosed, sourced reacceleration on the money-corner link net of the divestiture: HVP Delivery Devices net sales grew 29.0% in Q1 2026, and the CFO stated on the Q2 2026 call that the non-SmartDose-3.5 portion (>50% of Delivery Devices revenue) was 'up double digits in the quarter, led by SelfDose and Crystal Zenith' -- growth in the exact remaining device platforms this placement's role names, net of the line that was sold off.

A mechanically clean balance sheet funding aggressive capital return: Piotroski F-score 8 of 9 (STRONG), Beneish M-score -2.791 (CLEAN against the -1.78 review threshold), Altman Z 16.49 (SAFE), a net cash position (-0.31x net debt/EBITDA), and $454M of buybacks (1.8M shares) plus $32M of dividends paid through H1 2026 funded from operating cash flow that already covers capex.

The SmartDose 3.5mL divestiture (closed 2026-07-01, $112.5M) is margin-accretive, not just revenue-dilutive: the CFO characterized the sold line as having been 'dilutive in the first half of the year' and its removal worth '50 basis points of incremental margin for the full year,' meaning the device-platform book the market is now pricing is a smaller but cleaner, higher-margin slice than the one that drove the earlier growth prints.
bear: No figure anywhere on disk or disclosed by the company attributes a GLP-1 or self-injection revenue percentage to this exact link; the company discloses a clean 10%-of-total-company figure only for its OTHER, CROWDED placement (elastomer-closure-components), and this dive's own O1 profile independently carries disclosed_revenue_exposure: NULL for this placement. The bull case rests on qualitative language ('self-injection devices for obesity and diabetes') over a revenue base that just shrank by a disclosed ~4 points (SmartDose 3.5mL, sold to AbbVie, closed 2026-07-01). RED TEAM (2026-09-06) quantification: even reading the disclosed figures most generously, HVP Delivery Devices (~15% of FY2025 total company revenue, ~$461.1M) minus the divested SmartDose 3.5mL line (~4%, ~$123.0M) leaves the remaining device-platform book at roughly 11.0% of FY2025 total revenue (~$338.2M), of which the CFO's 'more than half... up double digits' language brackets the actual money-corner growth driver at roughly 5.5% of total company revenue (~$169.1M) or more, an UPPER bound because SelfDose and Crystal Zenith are named, multi-indication platforms, not GLP-1-exclusive, and no company disclosure separates GLP-1-specific revenue from other self-injection use within that sub-slice. Whether the actual GLP-1 dollar volume flowing through this link is a fraction of even that 5.5% ceiling, or whether GLP-1 volume growth's money accrues mainly to the drugmaker (Novo Nordisk, Eli Lilly) rather than to West's device/component fee, cannot be answered from the two files this red team is scoped to; no customer-concentration disclosure for the device-platform link is present in either file, which is a capture-reality data gap this dive's own data_gaps list did not yet name.

The expectations gap is horizon-fragile: the reverse-DCF ask at the ten-year explicit-period convention (18.34%) sits only 7.67 points above this dive's own 10.67% independent FCF-CAGR estimate, inside this file's own 14.62-point horizon_spread band, so the 22.29-point gap this dive claims exists only under the five-year convention; a market pricing this on a ten-year growth runway would not be measurably wrong by this file's own rule.

Mild earnings-quality and governance flags are stacking rather than isolated: days-sales-outstanding rose from 68.2 days at FY2025 to roughly 75.7-78.1 days annualized at H1 2026 (a 11-15% jump), deferred income fell 14.9% ($53.7M to $45.7M) over the same six months, and both the CFO (new August 2025) and the CEO (new effective 2026-08-31, five days before this dive) turned over within about thirteen months of each other, capping the earnings-quality grade at B rather than A despite a clean mechanical core.

rows.market_implied_note: The filed solve returns an FCF CAGR, not a decomposed revenue CAGR; the reverse_dcf block does not separate the two. This dive avoids the category mismatch a prior red team caught on this repo (comparing a revenue rate to an FCF rate) by building an independent revenue-to-FCF bridge instead, reserved for the net_gap_direction row below; this row records the revenue-specific assumption on its own terms.
rows.why: FY2026 guide (raised twice this year) implies +9.38% at the guided revenue-range midpoint ($3,362.5M vs FY2025's $3,074.1M); the trailing 3-year CAGR is only 2.1%. 7.5% sits between those two points: below the current guided pace (assuming GLP-1 comp effects and the SmartDose divestiture normalize growth over five years) but well above the trailing multi-year average, roughly at the top of the company's own previously stated long-term algorithm (an analyst reference to a prior 7-9% long-term target was found this run via WebSearch, INFERRED, not filing-verified).
rows.structural_reason: A real, disclosed, multi-quarter reacceleration (Q1 2026 organic +15.3%, Q2 2026 guide raised again) tied to GLP-1-linked demand, which this repo's own base rates (10-20% growers fall to 5-8% within five years) would put West's likely five-year path at the upper end of, not above, that band.
rows.leading_indicator: FY2026 organic sales growth landing at or above the raised 10-11% guided floor at the year-end release (watch_triggers[0]).

rows.market_implied_note: The filed solve does not decompose an operating-margin path separately from the headline FCF CAGR.
rows.why: FY2025 GAAP operating margin was 19.03%, and Q2 2026 adjusted operating margin already ran at 22.6% (per WebSearch this run, INFERRED). 22% by year five sits between the current GAAP level and the FY2021 COVID-cycle peak of 26.57% (752.3M/2831.6M), consistent with -- not exceeding -- management's own stated direction ('margin expansion should continue into 2027,' per WebSearch this run) plus the disclosed SmartDose-divestiture tailwind (+50bps FY2026).
rows.structural_reason: Mix shift toward higher-margin HVP/Delivery Devices revenue, the disclosed SmartDose 3.5mL divestiture margin accretion, and capex moderating from the FY2023-2024 peak ($362-377M) toward a guided $250-275M annual run rate as built capacity reaches utilization, per the Q2 2026 call (WebSearch this run, INFERRED).
rows.leading_indicator: Adjusted operating margin holding at or above 22% (the Q2 2026 print) through the FY2026 year-end release, rather than reverting toward the 19.03% FY2025 GAAP level.

rows.market_implied_note: The filed solve does not decompose a reinvestment return separately from the headline FCF CAGR, and no company-disclosed ROIC figure was found this run.
rows.why: A rough return on invested capital, computed here from fundamentals on disk (not disclosed by the company), fell from approximately 20.05% in FY2022 (NOPAT $579.86M at an assumed 21% tax rate, over invested capital $2,891.6M = long-term debt $206.7M + equity $2,684.9M) to approximately 13.68% in FY2025 (NOPAT $462.1M over invested capital $3,378.8M = long-term debt $202.8M + equity $3,176.0M), the trailing signature of the heavy FY2023-2024 capex build (capex/depreciation ran 2.36x-2.64x those years) landing ahead of revenue. 15% assumes only a partial recovery toward the 2022 level as utilization catches up to the built capacity, not a full round trip, which this repo's own base rate (roughly 40-50% of top-quartile ROIC firms stay there after ten years) argues against assuming without more evidence than a management comment on a call.
rows.structural_reason: Guided capex moderation ($250-275M annually vs $362-377M in FY2023-2024) alongside continued revenue growth would mechanically lift ROIC even without margin expansion, provided the built capacity is actually filled with demand rather than sitting idle.
rows.leading_indicator: FY2026 capex landing inside the guided $250-275M range (down from FY2025's $285.9M) while revenue growth holds at or above the raised guide, the combination that would mechanically lift ROIC without requiring a margin assumption beyond the operating_margin row above.

rows.why: No disagreement, and saying so matters. The solve's 2.5% perpetual growth sits at or below the long-run nominal GDP ceiling this repo's own base rates cite, and is not the input this dive would change for a specialty pharma-services supplier with real but not unlimited pricing power (capture score 72, a qualification-locked but partly private layer, per the chain's own heat rationale).

rows.note: Building like-for-like (revenue CAGR x steady-state margin x FY2025 cash conversion held constant, the same bridge ANDR.VI/688425.SS/ESLT used in this repo): 3,074.1M revenue compounding at 7.5% to 4,413.3M in FY2030; operating income at a 22% margin gives 970.9M against FY2025's 584.9M (+10.67% CAGR); holding the FY2025 FCF-to-operating-income ratio (468.9/584.9 = 0.8017) gives FY2030 free cash flow of 778.4M against the filed base of 468.9M, an FCF CAGR also of 10.67% (unchanged by the constant-conversion assumption, since it scales both numerator and denominator identically). Gap against the filed 5-year 32.96%: 22.29 points, well outside this file's own 14.62-point horizon_spread -- a real claimed gap, not a horizon-convention artifact, at this convention. At the 10-year convention (18.34% implied) the gap narrows to 7.67 points, INSIDE the horizon_spread, so by this file's own rule there is NO measurable gap at that duration: the sign does not flip, but the claim of a real gap does not survive every convention this dive can vary, unlike 688425.SS's record in this same log. Stress-tested on three further axes: (1) discount rate -- independently replicating quality.reverse_dcf's own bisection (reproduces the filed solve to three decimals: 32.963% vs 0.3296 at 5y, 24.386% vs 0.2439 at 7y, 18.337% vs 0.1834 at 10y) and lowering the discount rate to 7% still implies 22.30% at the 5-year horizon, an 11.63-point gap against 10.67%, wider than the horizon_spread and in the same direction, so the 5-year gap survives a lower discount rate; (2) FCF base -- the filed $468.9M base is 1.17x the FY2022-2025 trailing 4-year average ($399.8M), a materially smaller outlier than this log's recurring base-year defect class (MYRG 2.90x, 688425.SS 2.00x), and using the LOWER trailing-average base makes the market's implied ask WORSE, not better (37.53% at 5y instead of 32.96%), the same direction as ESLT, because West's FCF has been broadly rising rather than spiking off one outlier year; (3) cash conversion -- reverting the FY2025 conversion ratio (0.8017) to the FY2022-2025 four-year average (0.6246, the series runs 0.599/0.613/0.485/0.802, itself volatile) lowers my_fcf_cagr to 5.28% against the same 970.9M FY2030 operating income, WIDENING the 5-year gap to 27.68 points and leaving the 10-year gap (18.34% vs 5.28% = 13.06pp) still inside the 14.62pp horizon_spread. Net: the claimed gap is real and survives discount-rate and base stress at the 5-year convention, but is not robust across horizon conventions, which is why this dive is WATCH rather than INVESTABLE. RED TEAM (2026-09-06) cross-check: independently forward-solved the same bridge at the 10-year explicit-period convention using this dive's own 10.67% base case (rather than comparing CAGR points against the market's 18.34% 10-year ask alone): EV = price x 72,000,000 shares - $232.9M net cash gives a fair price of $193.67 at 10 years, still 43.4% below the $342.08 reference, against $148.13 (56.7% below) at the 5-year convention already used for the zone. Green's announced retirement, five days before this dive) turned over within about thirteen months of each other -- both orderly, multi-month-telegraphed successions rather than abrupt departures, but a double leadership transition in just over a year is still named plainly rather than smoothed over. Not A: flags (1) and (5) alone exceed grade A's threshold and clean-governance bar. Not C: none of the above is a Beneish breach, and neither the DSO nor the deferred-income move is confirmed as SUSTAINED (each is one data point against a prior flat or unconfirmed series); this dive could not independently verify a multi-year deferred-income series this run (data_gaps), which is itself named as a limit on how confidently grade B, rather than C, can be held. No related-party dealings beyond the disclosed, decades-old Daikyo relationship were found; that search was not exhaustive. The veto is not load-bearing on this dive: grade B caps nothing, and the verdict is WATCH on gap-horizon-fragility and independence-test grounds that would bind at grade A as well.

pre_mortem.premise: It is 2027-09-06, twelve months after this dive, and the WATCH call was wrong.
reasons: The market's extrapolation proved right rather than the dive's caution: FY2026 organic growth held at or above the raised 10-11% guided floor through year-end, the non-SmartDose-3.5 Delivery Devices business kept compounding at 'double digits' or better into FY2027, and a third and fourth consecutive guidance raise closed the gap between the market's 32.96% five-year FCF-CAGR ask and this dive's own 10.67% base case faster than the reverse-DCF math implied was likely. In hindsight the 82%-buy-rating sell-side consensus this dive's crowdedness section flagged as a tension, rather than a contradiction, would have been the better read of the evidence, and staying at WATCH through the October 2026 and subsequent quarters meant missing a continuation of a still-early re-rating.

The bear case realized and the WATCH should have named a hard ceiling instead of leaving no_entry_above null: FY2026 organic growth printed at or below the 10% floor (watch_triggers[0]), the non-SmartDose device business decelerated below 'double digits' (watch_triggers[1]), and deferred income kept falling past $45.7M (watch_triggers[2]), confirming that Q1-Q2 2026's reacceleration was a comp-driven spike (partly the now-divested SmartDose 3.5mL line, partly a GLP-1 demand pull-forward) rather than a durable structural shift, at which point the stock, still carrying a rich forward multiple, corrected sharply from $342.08 toward or through this dive's own would-buy zone within the 90-day COMPOUNDER clock, and this dive's own entry-basis-stress finding (that the zone is a base-case-fair floor, not a bear-survived one) meant the drawn zone still overpaid relative to the bear case that actually played out.

An idiosyncratic, leadership-driven event overtook the GLP-1 thesis this dive is built around: the new CEO (Michel Lagarde, five days into the role at this dive's as_of date) used the balance-sheet strength this dive's earnings-quality section already documents (net cash, Piotroski 8/9, $454M of buybacks already executed in H1 2026) for a large acquisition or further portfolio reshaping that changed West's growth algorithm, margin mix, or capital-allocation story in a direction this dive's GLP-1-device-platform framework never modeled, making the entire expectations-gap table's premise, that West in twelve months looks like West today plus GLP-1 volume growth, stale regardless of which way GLP-1 demand itself went.
pre_mortem.why_the_market_could_have_been_right: Reason 1 is the most concrete and directly tied to this file's own falsification design: the independence_test's own trigger (FY2026 organic growth at or above the raised 10-11% floor, non-SmartDose device growth holding at 'double digits' or better) is exactly the evidence that would validate the market's extrapolation rather than this dive's 10.67% base case, and the real, disclosed, multi-quarter reacceleration already on record (Q1 2026 organic +15.3%, two consecutive guidance raises) is not manufactured evidence for this pre-mortem; it is already in bull[0]. A GLP-1 self-injection device market still in its early volume-ramp years is a structural setup where a supplier's growth can plausibly outrun a diversified components company's own trailing multi-year average for longer than five years, which is precisely the base-rate question this dive's own percentile scoring (65 for revenue CAGR) already flags as sitting toward the upper, not the extreme, end of defensible outcomes.
pre_mortem.downgrade_note: The verdict is already at WATCH, the floor an unanswerable pre-mortem would impose, and a coherent, filing-grounded market-would-have-been-right story is namable and ties directly to this file's own falsification trigger, so the pre-mortem informs the file without forcing further change, the same non-effect this analyst's log recorded for HUBB, MYRG and ESLT.

red_team.surviving_bear_case: West's exposure to GLP-1-linked device-platform demand is real and disclosed at the issuer level, but this dive's own link (autoinjector-and-pen-platforms) has no company-disclosed revenue percentage attached to it, and this red team's own quantification of the dive's cited figures brackets the actual growth-driving sub-slice at an upper bound of roughly 5.5% of total company revenue, with no way to confirm how much of that is GLP-1-specific versus other self-injection indications, or how much of GLP-1 volume growth's dollar value reaches West's device fee rather than the drugmaker. The market's own reverse-DCF ask, a 32.96% five-year FCF CAGR against this dive's defended 10.67% base case, survives discount-rate and FCF-base stress and, this red team confirms, survives in dollar terms even at the gentler 10-year convention (43.4% below spot) despite the CAGR-point gap there sitting inside the file's own horizon_spread noise band. The market's reaction to two comparably-sized 2026 guidance raises collapsed from +12.86% in April to +1.74% in July, evidence the reacceleration story is already substantially absorbed rather than freshly discovered. And the would-buy zone this dive draws to make INVESTABLE testable ($148.13-$162.54) turns out, under this red team's own bear-case rebuild, to price the file's base case rather than a level that has already absorbed the bear case named in this same file, so a buyer waiting for that zone is still buying above-trend growth and margin expansion, not a demonstrated margin of safety. None of this is a books-quality problem (grade B, mechanically clean, mild and each-disclosed flags only) or a crowdedness problem sufficient on its own (the link-level UNDISCOVERED read is contestable but not reversed by anything on disk this pass); it is a valuation-and-attribution finding, which is exactly what keeps this file at WATCH rather than TOO_LATE (guidance has been raised roughly in step with price, an estimate-revision story) or INVESTABLE (the independence test's own falsification window, Q3 2026 results around 2026-10-30, has not yet fired in either direction).
